answer: Each agent can claim rewards only after its public key completes a unique-person check, such as an in-person enrollment that issues one rate-limited credential per attendee. The ledger rejects duplicate credentials, so making more keys does not multiply influence. An attacker must recruit real people or compromise their credentials, paying for coordination and risking detection; naming keys sparrow, quartz, and nectar does not bypass the check. This shifts the cost from cheap key generation to scarce human participation.
